arxiv-2211-00084.title: An explicit exponential time integrator based on Faber polynomials and its application to seismic wave modelling
arxiv-2211-00084.creator: Fernando V. Ravelo, Pedro S. Peixoto, Martin Schreiber
arxiv-2211-00084.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Fernando V. Ravelo, Pedro S. Peixoto, Martin Schreiber. Exponential time integrators have been applied successfully in several physics-related differential equations. However, their application in hyperbolic systems with absorbing boundaries, like the ones arising in seismic imaging, still lacks theoretical and experimental investigations. The present work conducts an in-depth study of exponential integration using Faber polynomials, consisting of a generalization of a popular exponential method that uses Chebyshev polynomials. This allows solving non-symmetric operators that emerge from classic seismic wave propagation problems with absorbing boundaries.

arxiv-2311-18123.title: Symmetries and Wavefunctions of Photons Confined in 3D Photonic Band Gap Superlattices
arxiv-2311-18123.creator: Marek Kozoň, Ad Lagendijk, Matthias Schlottbom, Jaap J. W. van der Vegt, Willem L. Vos
arxiv-2311-18123.description: Abstract We perform a computational study of confined photonic states that appear in a three-dimensional (3D) superlattice of coupled cavities, resulting from a superstructure of intentional defects. The states are isolated from the vacuum by a 3D photonic band gap, using a diamond-like inverse woodpile crystal structure, and exhibit ’Cartesian’ hopping of photons in high-symmetry directions.

arxiv-2405-14329.title: A confined random walk locally looks like tilted random interlacements
arxiv-2405-14329.creator: Nicolas Bouchot
arxiv-2405-14329.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Nicolas Bouchot. In this paper we consider the simple random walk on ℤ d \mathbb{Z}^{d} , d ≥ 3 d\geq 3 , conditioned to stay forever in a large domain D N D_{N} of typical diameter N N . Considering the range up to time t N ≥ N 2 + δ t_{N}\geq N^{2+\delta} for some δ > 0 \delta>0 , we establish a coupling with what Li & Sznitman [ LS14 ] defined as tilted random interlacements .

arxiv-2406-05867.title: GANSky – fast curved sky weak lensing simulations using Generative Adversarial Networks
arxiv-2406-05867.creator: Supranta S. Boruah, Pier Fiedorowicz, Rafael Garcia, William R. Coulton, Eduardo Rozo, Giulio Fabbian
arxiv-2406-05867.description: Abstract Extracting non-Gaussian information from the next generation weak lensing surveys will require fast and accurate full-sky simulations. This is difficult to achieve in practice with existing simulation methods: ray-traced N N -body simulations are computationally expensive, and approximate simulation methods (such as lognormal mocks) are not accurate enough.

arxiv-2409-05828.title: Many-Body Dephasing by Hole Motion in a Spin-Orbit-Coupled Mott Insulator
arxiv-2409-05828.creator: Alexis Ghermaoui, Manel Bosch Aguilera, Raphaël Bouganne, Rémy Vatré, Isabella Fritsche, Jérôme Beugnon, Fabrice Gerbier
arxiv-2409-05828.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Alexis Ghermaoui, Manel Bosch Aguilera, Raphaël Bouganne, Rémy Vatré, Isabella Fritsche, Jérôme Beugnon, Fabrice Gerbier. We use Ramsey interferometry to study spin dynamics in the strongly interacting regime of spin-orbit-coupled quantum gases in one-dimensional optical lattices. We observe an intrinsic many-body dephasing mechanism immune to spin-echo in two-component Mott insulators. We ascribe the dephasing to the motion of hole-like defects in an otherwise inert Mott insulator, the spinless nature of the holes explaining the ineffectiveness of spin echo to restore it.

arxiv-2410-20041.title: Sparse Linear Bandits with Blocking Constraints
arxiv-2410-20041.creator: Adit Jain, Soumyabrata Pal, Sunav Choudhary, Ramasuri Narayanam, Harshita Chopra, Vikram Krishnamurthy
arxiv-2410-20041.description: Abstract We investigate the high-dimensional sparse linear bandits problem in a data-poor regime where the time horizon is much smaller than the ambient dimension and number of arms. We study the setting under the additional blocking constraint where each unique arm can be pulled only once.

arxiv-2509-02055.title: Align-Then-stEer: Adapting the Vision-Language Action Models through Unified Latent Guidance
arxiv-2509-02055.creator: Yang Zhang, Chenwei Wang, Ouyang Lu, Yuan Zhao, Yunfei Ge, Zhenglong Sun, Xiu Li, Chi Zhang, Chenjia Bai, Xuelong Li
arxiv-2509-02055.description: Abstract Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models pre-trained on large, diverse datasets show remarkable potential for general-purpose robotic manipulation. However, a primary bottleneck remains in adapting these models to downstream tasks, especially when the robot’s embodiment or the task itself differs from the pre-training data. This discrepancy leads to a significant mismatch in action distributions, demanding extensive data and compute for effective fine-tuning.

arxiv-2510-23210.title: Higher order numerical schemes for SPDEs with additive Noise
arxiv-2510-23210.creator: Abhishek Chaudhary, Andreas Prohl
arxiv-2510-23210.description: Abstract We present high-order numerical schemes for linear stochastic heat and wave equations with Dirichlet boundary conditions, driven by additive noise. Standard Euler schemes for SPDEs are limited to an order convergence between 1 / 2 1/2 and 1 1 due to the low temporal regularity of noise.

arxiv-2511-08748.title: WiCV at CVPR 2025: The Women in Computer Vision Workshop
arxiv-2511-08748.creator: Estefania Talavera, Deblina Bhattacharjee, Himangi Mittal, Mengwei Ren, Karen Sanchez, Carla Muntean, JungEun Kim, Mona Jalal
arxiv-2511-08748.description: Abstract The Women in Computer Vision Workshop (WiCV@CVPR 2025) was held in conjunction with the IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (CVPR 2025) in Nashville, Tennessee, United States. This report presents an overview of the workshop program, participation statistics, mentorship outcomes, and historical trends from previous WiCV editions.

pmc-11413719.title: Diagnostic Efficacy of Ultrasound-Based International Ovarian Tumor Analysis Simple Rules and Assessment of the Different Neoplasias in the Adnexa Model in Malignancy Prediction Among Women With Adnexal Masses: A Systematic Review
pmc-11413719.creator: Shweta V Suryawanshi, Kanchan S Dwidmuthe, Snehal Savalkar, Anuja Bhalerao
pmc-11413719.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Transvaginal ultrasonography (USG) is most commonly used before surgery to accurately diagnose benign and malignant ovarian masses for effective treatment, avoid unnecessary interventions, improve the prognosis of patients, and preserve fertility in patients with benign tumors. Therefore, the objective of the present systematic review was to assess the diagnostic efficacy of ultrasound-based International Ovarian Tumor Analysis (IOTA) Simple Rules (SR) and Assessment of Different NEoplasias in the adneXa (ADNEX) model in predicting malignancy among women with adnexal masses.

pmc-11655203.title: The neuronal Golgi in neural circuit formation and reorganization
pmc-11655203.creator: Naoki Nakagawa
pmc-11655203.description: The Golgi apparatus is a central hub in the intracellular secretory pathway. By positioning in the specific intracellular region and transporting materials to spatially restricted compartments, the Golgi apparatus contributes to the cell polarity establishment and morphological specification in diverse cell types.

pmc-11656912.title: Application of deep learning in wound size measurement using fingernail as the reference
pmc-11656912.creator: Dun-Hao Chang, Duc-Khanh Nguyen, Thi-Ngoc Nguyen, Chien-Lung Chan
pmc-11656912.description: ObjectiveMost current wound size measurement devices or applications require manual wound tracing and reference markers. Chronic wound care usually relies on patients or caregivers who might have difficulties using these devices. Considering a more human-centered design, we propose an automatic wound size measurement system by combining three deep learning (DL) models and using fingernails as a reference.

pmc-12405548.title: Remaining useful life prediction of lithium–ion batteries via spatial attention TLSTM and dilated CNN with evolutionary optimization
pmc-12405548.creator: Suhua Chen, Xu Fang
pmc-12405548.description: The precise estimation of the Remaining Useful Life (RUL) of lithium–ion batteries is essential for averting unforeseen failures and enhancing operational efficiency and maintenance planning. This paper presents an advanced deep learning framework that couples a spatial-attention mechanism with a Transductive Long Short-Term Memory (TLSTM) model, augmented by one-dimensional dilated convolutional layers to capture long-range temporal dependencies.

pmc-12655792.title: Comparison of the Intestinal Microbiota of Patients with Urticaria and Healthy Controls: The Role of Blastocystis
pmc-12655792.creator: Nurullah Ciftci, Salih Macin, Gülcan Saylam Kurtipek, Uğur Arslan, Fabrizio Bruschi, Geoff Hide
pmc-12655792.description: Urticaria is a skin disorder characterized by erythematous, edematous, and pruritic lesions. Intestinal microorganisms can trigger various immunological responses, and Blastocystis has been suggested to affect gut-associated lymphoid tissue homeostasis and induce allergic reactions. This study aimed to evaluate the effect of Blastocystis on the intestinal microbiota in patients with urticaria.

pmc-12722959.title: Circuitry correlates of negative urgency and suicidality in schizophrenia spectrum disorders: a LASSO regression study
pmc-12722959.creator: Tyler Pia, Enna Sanghvi, Mark Shuquan Chen, Thomas Kim, Matthew J. Hoptman, Anthony O. Ahmed
pmc-12722959.description: ObjectiveSuicidality is highly prevalent with vast public health implications. The association between schizophrenia spectrum disorders (SSDs) and suicidal ideation and related behaviors (SIBs) is well established. One construct that has received less attention is emotion-based impulsivity or urgency, defined as impulsive action in the context of high positive or negative emotion states.

pmc-12734134.title: Antifungal Susceptibility and Resistance-Associated Gene Expression in Nosocomial Candida Isolates
pmc-12734134.creator: Fabiola Berenice Hernandez-Reyes, Luis Alfonso Muñoz-Miranda, Manuel R Kirchmayr, Pablo César Ortiz-Lazareno, Rafael Cortés-Zárate, Maricarmen Iñiguez-Moreno, Heriberto Jacobo-Cuevas, Cesar Arturo Nava-Valdivia, Jose Luis Lopez-Ribot
pmc-12734134.description: Background: Nosocomial infections represent a significant clinical burden due to high morbidity, mortality and healthcare costs. Invasive fungal infections, particularly those caused by Candida species, are of growing concern due to increasing antifungal resistance, which limits therapeutic options and worsens patient outcomes.

pmc-12949932.title: LOX - 1 gene knockout improves metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis in mice
pmc-12949932.creator: Ruihua HUANG, Yongyu YANG, Shuhan ZHOU, Xiaoyun ZHU, Changping HU, Minning PENG
pmc-12949932.description: ObjectiveMetabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH), a progressive subtype of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), is characterized by hepatic steatosis, lobular inflammation, and hepatocyte ballooning, and may further progress to liver fibrosis and cirrhosis. Lectin-like oxidized low-density lipoprotein receptor-1 (LOX-1), a member of the scavenger receptor family, recognizes and binds oxidized low-density lipoprotein.

pmc-13079344.title: Elephant-derived Bacillus licheniformis modulates immune cells shedding light on cancer resistance
pmc-13079344.creator: Xiaoyi Wang, Min Wei, Yang Yi, Jiaming An, Jingjing Wang, Rongjie Zhao, Zhan Su, Guozhong Ji, Xuemei Zhang, Xingyin Liu
pmc-13079344.description: IntroductionColorectal cancer (CRC) is currently a leading cause of cancer-related morbidity and mortality globally, underscoring the need for innovative therapeutic strategies. Probiotic treatment is increasingly appreciated as an innovative method for ameliorating inflammation and modulating the tumor microenvironment, especially in gastrointestinal diseases. Many bacterial species isolated from human and animal sources are proven effective in potential disease treatments.

pmc-13326037.title: Multi‐Enzyme Mimetic Molybdenum Nitride Nanozymes Reshape Subgingival Microenvironment for Synergistic Periodontitis Therapy via ROS Regulation and Microbiome Remodeling
pmc-13326037.creator: Weiyu Zhang, Zhongwei Yang, Yunfan Zhang, Longwei Wang, Xiaoyu Zhang, Jiahui Mao, Yizhi Dai, Yifan Yuan, Mingge Wang, Xin Yang, Xin Yu, Jing Liu, Chunying Chen
pmc-13326037.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Periodontitis, a chronic inflammatory disease initiated and sustained by plaque microorganisms and host immune response, remains an intractable oral disease and a leading cause of tooth loss worldwide. Traditional mechanical debridement and adjunctive antibiotic or antiseptic therapy often shows limited efficacy due to the complex anatomical structure, concerns regarding antimicrobial resistance, and poor penetration and retention within the subgingival infection niche.

pmc-13427754.title: A miniature piezoelectric-thermomagnetic generator for low-grade waste heat recovery
pmc-13427754.creator: Maxim Wischnewski, Joel Joseph, Makoto Ohtsuka, Hiroyuki Miki, Manfred Kohl
pmc-13427754.description: This paper presents the experimental and model-based investigation of a compact miniature-size generator for conversion of low-grade waste heat at temperatures near 100 °C to electricity leveraging the combined transducer effects of a thermomagnetic (TM) and a piezoelectric (P) layer.

pmc-13631548.title: Detection of zoonotic bacteria in wild Australian freshwater turtles
pmc-13631548.creator: TF Scheelings, TTH Van, RJ Moore, LF Skerratt
pmc-13631548.description: Freshwater turtles are long‐lived, abundant components of Australian aquatic ecosystems, yet little is known about the diversity and prevalence of zoonotic bacteria they may carry. In this study, we conducted one of the most comprehensive surveys to date of zoonotic microorganisms associated with wild Australian freshwater turtles.
